Open Start and type your studio name and your own limits in the yellow cells: mark-up, reserve, target margin, item margin share, long-lead weeks, sample days and waste share.
Check Projects, Rooms (Room budgets) and Vendors. They hold the projects, the approved room budgets and the vendors that every other sheet looks up.
Fill Mark-up rules with the standard and the minimum mark-up of each category and the rounding step; Discount tiers with the extra discounts each vendor gives.
Enter each item on FF&E schedule: project, room, vendor, quantity, list price, trade discount and mark-up. Unit cost, client price, margin and the checks fill in.
Watch Room budgets and Project budgets: the specified total, what is left, the over-budget check and the reserve update with every item you add.
Use Budget by category and Allowances to compare the specification with the category shares and with the allowance agreed with the client.
Log asks on Specification approvals, samples on Finish and samples, and stuck items on Decisions. Days waiting and the checks show what to chase.
Record each Substitutions row and each Alternatives option so the price, margin and lead-time effect is clear before you write to the client.
Keep Dimensions, Lighting schedule and Fabric schedule up to date for sizes, watts, metres and order dates.
Use the 14 calculators for prices, mark-up, room and category budgets, substitutions, quantity tiers, fabric, flooring, lighting, rounding, cuts, the reserve and what-ifs.
Read the Specification Dashboard and Charts every week: specified value, margin, rooms over budget, substitutions, samples and items waiting.
Order everything your clients approved, on time and at the right price

Purchase orders with trade cost, client price and payments
One row per purchase order: vendor, dates, trade cost, client price, deposit and balance; the margin, mark-up, days late, late flag and the deposit and balance state fill in by themselves.
Order lines with trade cost, client price and margin
A sample of order lines: item, quantity, trade cost and client price per unit; the line cost, line price, margin and the vendor and project of the order fill in by themselves.
Procurement tracker with status and next action
One row per purchase order: when the vendor confirmed, started production and shipped; the status, promise, days in status and the next action fill in by themselves.
Approved items waiting to be ordered with the order-by date
One row per approved item that is not yet on a placed order: vendor, lead time and the date the client needs it; the order-by date, days left and an order flag fill in by themselves.
Vendor payments with due date, days late and open amount
One row per payment to a vendor: kind, amount, due date and paid date; the days late, the payment flag, the open amount and the project fill in by themselves.
Vendor deposits and balances due by vendor and month
One row per vendor and month: deposits and balances that fell due and what was paid; the total due, the open amount, the paid share and a flag fill in by themselves.
Vendor accounts with discount, terms and open balance
One row per vendor or trade account: discount, deposit share, terms and lead time; the open orders, open balance, overdue and disputed amounts and the orders this year fill in by themselves.
Vendor quotes with validity and days to expiry
One row per vendor quote: project, what was quoted, price and validity; the days to expiry, a flag for quotes about to lapse and the project name fill in by themselves.
Order confirmations checked against the purchase order
One row per vendor confirmation: the total and lead time the vendor confirmed; the order total, the price and lead time change, the difference and whether it matches fill in by themselves.
Back-orders and delays with new promise and client notice
One row per back-order or delay: reason, old and new promise and when the client was told; the days of delay, vendor, project, client phone and a notice check fill in by themselves.
Projects with lead, status, FF&E budget and ordered value
One row per project with the lead, status, dates and FF&E budget; the number of orders, the ordered value at client price and the share of the FF&E ordered fill in by themselves.
Orders by project with margin and what is not yet ordered
One row per project: the value of approved items still to order; the orders placed, trade cost, client price, margin, the budget check and the share ordered fill in by themselves.
FF&E invoices to the client against what was ordered
One row per FF&E invoice: project, kind and amount billed; the project billed so far, the trade cost and client price ordered, the gap and a billing flag fill in by themselves.
Freight and handling with quote, actual and insurance
One row per delivered or shipped order: carrier, freight quote, actual charge and insurance; the freight share of the order, the variance against the quote and a flag fill in by themselves.
Lead time book by vendor category with buffer
One row per vendor category: typical, shortest and longest lead weeks and your buffer; the planning weeks, the weeks seen on delivered orders and a flag fill in by themselves.
Cancelled and changed orders with fee and net change
One row per change or cancellation after an order: what changed, the old and new total, any fee and who approved it; the net change, vendor and a flag fill in by themselves.
Credits and returns with amount and open credit flag
One row per credit or return asked from a vendor: item, reason, amount and the date the credit arrived; the vendor, project, open credit flag and days open fill in by themselves.
Reorder and top-up list for short or damaged items
One row per short, damaged or added item to buy again: quantity, reason, vendor and the order that bought it; the value, vendor phone and whether the reorder is placed fill in by themselves.
Weekly calendar with deposits, balances and cash needed
One row per week: the client receipts expected; the orders to place, deposits and balances due to vendors, items reaching their order-by date and the cash needed fill in from the other sheets.
Team with roles, hour cost, bill rate and projects led
The owner designer, four staff and seven freelance specialists with role, hours and rates; the margin per hour and the active projects each person leads fill in by themselves.
